title: Handling body fluid spills and contaminated sharps
moduleTitle: Caregiving: infection control (no course slug assigned)
audience: Caregivers and supervisors who may respond to body fluid spills or handle used sharps in personal care
learningOutcomes: Isolate and protect an area before cleaning a body fluid spill
Clean and disinfect a spill using the approved product's label and the organisation's procedure
Handle, contain and report a used sharp and any contact with fluids from the body

instruction.heading: Isolate and protect first
instruction.body: When a body fluid spill occurs, the first task is to isolate the area and protect yourself. Keep others away, and dress in gloves, a waterproof apron and goggles. If the spill is large, a person is hurt, or the situation is beyond the procedure you have been trained for, stop and call for help through the escalation route. This lesson does not authorise work beyond your training.

instruction.heading: Clean and disinfect using the product label
instruction.body: Blot the fluid using disposable paper towel or the product the procedure names. Where the procedure calls for a chlorine-releasing granular product, cover the spill and leave it for the contact time on the label. Collect the waste, bag it, clean the surface using hot, soapy water, dry it, and then dispose of towels and gloves. The source gives a bleach dilution and contact time, and this lesson does not reproduce them. The dilution and contact time must come from the approved product's label and the organisation's procedure. Never mix cleaning products.

instruction.heading: Sharps: contain, do not recap
instruction.body: Never recap, bend or break a used needle. Handle the sharp by its barrel and place it straight into a puncture-resistant sharps container. Do not overfill the container. The source refers to container standards and a yellow labelling scheme.

instruction.heading: After an exposure: flush, report, record, seek advice
instruction.body: If blood or body fluid reaches your skin, rinse the skin under running water, wash it with lukewarm water and a mild soap, and tell the responsible person about it. Record it in the organisation's incident system and seek medical advice. The source names a specific incident form.

procedure: Stop, isolate the area and keep others away.
Dress in gloves, a waterproof apron and goggles.
Absorb or contain the fluid and place the waste in a bag.
Disinfect the area using the product and contact time on its label and the organisation's procedure.
Clean with hot, soapy water, dry, dispose of the items, and wash your hands.
For a sharp, use the container. For an exposure, flush, report, record and seek advice.

workedExamples.situation: A carer finds a small spill of urine with a few drops of blood in a bathroom after a client's nosebleed, and a used disposable razor on the floor.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must happen, and in what order?
workedExamples.reasoning: Isolate the bathroom and dress in gloves, apron and goggles. Pick up the razor with a tool, or by its handle, into a sharps container. Absorb and disinfect the spill using the approved product and its label. Clean, dry, dispose of the waste, wash hands, and report the sharp and any contact with the blood.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves: heavy-duty for cleaning, single-use for contact

commonErrors.error: Cleaning a spill with bare hands or without eye protection
commonErrors.prevention: Put on the full PPE set before touching the spill.
Use only the named product, and never mix products.
Flush, report and record at once.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Do not mix cleaning products, and do not combine a bleach-based product with other chemicals.
The bleach dilution and contact time in the source are not reproduced or relied on. The approved product label and the organisation's procedure apply.
This lesson does not grant authority to handle clinical waste or carry out regulated decontamination, and does not grant any licence. Do not clean beyond your training; escalate.

qualityStandard: Area isolated and PPE on before cleaning starts
Disinfection follows the product label and procedure, with contact time met
Sharp contained without recapping, and exposure reported and recorded the same shift
documentationEvidence: Incident report for each spill involving blood or body fluid
Exposure record with first aid and advice given
summary: Disinfect by the product label and procedure, never from memory.
Never recap a sharp; report every exposure.

knowledgeChecks.question: The first action when a body fluid spill happens is to:
options: Wipe it with bare hands to clear it fast and well
Isolate the area and dress in gloves, apron and goggles
Wash the floor with cold water only and the mop

knowledgeChecks.question: A used needle should be:
options: Recapped to be safe, put back on the trolley for the next use in the room
Bent to save space in the bin, the trolley, the cart and the drawer
Handled by the barrel and placed in a puncture-resistant container

knowledgeChecks.question: Which source should set the disinfectant dilution and contact time for a spill?
options: A guess from memory of the last spill at the house or the ward
The approved product label and the organisation's procedure
The colour of the bottle, the lid, the label and the shape
